what: Vertex Pharmaceuticals develops medicines for diseases caused by a single faulty gene. Its cystic fibrosis drugs, led by Trikafta and the newer Alyftrek, treat the large majority of people with the disease worldwide and provide almost all of the company's revenue.
customers: Health systems, insurers and national health services that pay for its medicines, prescribed by specialist doctors.
money: Trikafta/Kaftrio, Alyftrek and earlier combinations, taken daily for life
a one-time gene-editing treatment for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, developed with CRISPR Therapeutics
a non-opioid painkiller approved for acute pain
moat: Patents and two decades of clinical know-how in cystic fibrosis, a disease where it has no direct competitor, plus deep relationships with the specialist clinics that treat patients.
rivals: Large pharmaceutical companies entering gene therapy
risks: Revenue still depends overwhelmingly on cystic fibrosis; a safety problem or a rival drug would hit hard
Key patents expire over the next decade
New launches outside cystic fibrosis have to prove they can replace that concentration
Price pressure from governments and US drug-pricing rules
opportunities: Alyftrek can extend the cystic fibrosis franchise with once-daily dosing and fresh patent life
Journavx addresses acute pain, a very large market where the alternative is opioids
Casgevy and the pipeline in kidney disease and pain could add revenue that does not depend on cystic fibrosis
watch: Whether Journavx prescriptions scale, and how quickly patients switch from Trikafta to Alyftrek.
